channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Live: French anti-terrorism prosecutor to give press conference on racist Paris shooting
item.description: A shooter suspected of killing one person and wounding five others last week in the town of Trappes, near Paris, was transferred to the Paris Judicial Court on Thursday, where he may be formally charged. France's national anti-terrorism prosecutor Olivier Christen is due to speak Thursday at 11am, with his statement to be broadcast live on FRANCE 24.

item.title: Billionaire tax, transgender rights, voter access among key midterm ballot measures
item.description: Voters will weigh in on several key ballot measures in the midterm elections.

item.title: How AI drones are influencing the course of the Ukraine war
item.description: Artificial intelligence is making drones faster and more capable. Russia and Ukraine both use AI-powered drones, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned that AI could lead decisions on the battlefield as soon as next year.

item.title: These are the House races to watch in the 2026 midterm election on Nov. 3
item.description: An NPR analysis finds 70 House districts where Democrats and Republicans are each investing more than six figures in advertising during the final few days of the election, including in deep red areas.

item.title: Tariffs, diesel and computer chips are driving up costs for automakers
item.description: American auto companies say they are paying more for key components like computer chips, steel and copper — plus the fuel needed to transport their products.

item.title: Business as a liberal art? Some high schools say yes
item.description: Learning about money is becoming a growing part of the high school curriculum.

item.title: Their colleges closed, but the government refuses to erase their debts, lawsuit says
item.description: Federal law requires the Education Department to erase the student loans of borrowers whose colleges close suddenly. A new lawsuit claims the department isn't fully following those rules.

item.title: Details of more than 40,000 Homeland Security workers leaked in major hack
item.description: Details of more than 40,000 Department of Homeland Security (DHS) employees have been leaked to the public.

item.title: 'Desolation, despair': Spain begins three days of mourning after deadly train crash
item.description: Spain entered three days of mourning on Thursday after a high-speed train collision killed 68 people and injured scores. The incident has prompted fresh questions about rail safety and management.

item.title: Spain reckons with 2nd deadly train crash of the year ahead of national election
item.description: Spain's second high-speed rail disaster this year, a crash in which one train struck another from behind, killing 68 people, has raised fresh concerns about the safety of the country's rail network.

item.title: League Cup: Liverpool edge Chelsea in penalty shoot-out
item.description: Liverpool reached the League Cup quarter-finals after eliminating Chelsea on penalties (6-5), following a 1-1 draw. Wesley Fofana sealed the Blues' exit by sending his spot-kick well over the bar. Another French defender at Chelsea, Maxence Lacroix, went off injured before half-time, a week before the France squad is announced.

item.title: North Korea fires 'around a dozen' ballistic missiles amid rising tensions with South Korea
item.description: North Korea fired around a dozen short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast on Thursday, Seoul's defence ministry said. The North Korean capital Pyongyang has stepped up weapons tests in recent weeks despite South Korea's offer of military talks.

item.title: WATCH: Long Island couple sues over real estate broker’s allegedly racist text
item.description: ABC News’ Linsey Davis speaks with a Long Island couple suing a now-former broker at realtor Douglas Elliman for housing discrimination, after the broker sent a text saying “Ugh they are black.”

item.title: Live: Israelis await final election results, with no majority in sight
item.description: With more than 90% of the ballots counted on Thursday, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc has gained 53 seats, with the opposition at 67, including 48 for Gadi Eisenkot's centrist bloc and 19 for the Arab-majority parties. The Israeli president called on the parties on Wednesday to "do everything" to form a government coalition and avoid a return to the polls. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Trump warned $10bn BBC lawsuit could be dismissed
item.description: Donald Trump's $10bn (£7.5bn) defamation lawsuit against the BBC could be dismissed unless he turns over documents requested by the broadcaster, a US court has warned.

item.title: Brewers beat the Rays 4-1 to win the first World Series title in franchise history
item.description: The small-ball Milwaukee Brewers playing in the smallest market in the majors are World Series champions for the first time in franchise history

item.title: 2 right-wing provocateurs facing election-related charges in Minnesota
item.description: Right-wing provocateurs James O'Keefe and Cam Higby are facing election-related charges after posting videos intended to expose alleged election security deficiencies.

item.title: Girl injured in wolf attack at wildlife park
item.description: An eight-year-old girl has been seriously injured in a wolf attack at a wildlife park in Germany.

item.title: Police close investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death
item.description: Police have closed the investigation into Hayden Panettiere's death after a post-mortem found she died accidentally.

item.title: Canada and EU drop associate membership plan in bid to deepen ties
item.description: Canada and the European Union will pursue closer ties but have dropped a proposal for associate EU membership, according to a joint declaration ahead of Thursday’s summit in Montreal. Prime Minister Mark Carney is seeking to reduce Canada’s reliance on the US, despite warnings from Donald Trump.

item.title: Peltola campaign under fire after report it recruited 2nd Dan Sullivan in Senate race
item.description: Alaskans for Mary said it "has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign."

item.title: Early vote one week out shows Democratic enthusiasm in Texas, Georgia: Analysis
item.description: With just one week out to the 2026 midterms, an ABC News analysis of the early vote in the key states of Texas and Georgia shows signs of enthusiasm for Democrats.

item.title: WATCH: David Muir remembers the life and legacy of Barbara Barrie
item.description: The Oscar, Emmy and Tony nominee appeared in numerous films and TV series, including her role as the supportive mother in “Breaking Away.” David Muir remembers her legacy.

item.title: WATCH: Netherlands zookeeper mauled in deadly leopard attack
item.description: An experienced zookeeper in the Netherlands has died after being mauled by a leopard during her morning rounds at the enclosures.

item.title: US makes interest rate decision - as Bank of England verdict looms
item.description: The Federal Reserve has left interest rates unchanged - despite persistently high inflation and repeated calls from Donald Trump to lower borrowing costs.

item.title: Dolores Huerta, civil rights icon, dies at 96
item.description: Dolores Huerta, who co-founded the United Farm Workers, has died at 96, her family said.

item.title: Some wellness peptides will become widely available, HHS says
item.description: "The policy does not ... establish clinical safety and effectiveness," HHS said.

item.title: Spain rail crash came after train ordered to go in error: minister
item.description: A rail collision in Spain that claimed at least 68 lives on Wednesday came after a train was ordered to go in "error" despite a technical failure that halted all services, the transport minister said. The first findings about the accident in the central region of Castilla-La Mancha are likely to revive questions about rail safety in Spain after another high-speed collision in January killed 46 people. FRANCE 24's James Vasina reports.

item.title: Midterm elections live updates: Trump heads to Ohio, Obama rallies in Georgia
item.description: Trump heads to Ohio to rally with candidates in competitive races in the state.

item.title: Flavio Bolsonaro claims he is Brazil's true leader after fleeing to US
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro insisted Wednesday he is his country's rightful leader after arriving in the United States to start a self-imposed exile. Bolsonaro's defiance on fleeing to Florida signaled continued upheaval for Brazil, where leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a dramatic runoff election Sunday. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Fabio de Sa e Silva, Associate Professor of International Studies at the University of Oklahoma. He says that an attempt by Bolsonaro to turn a domestic dispute into a wider international issue "will not be successful", explaining that he is likely going to be "losing the grip of the opposition, there is a vacuum now that others will seek to occupy" and that it's unlikely that the United States will "get involved into questioning the results of the Brazilian election".

item.title: Rail safety questioned after Spain suffers second fatal high-speed train crash in a year
item.description: Questions are being raised about Spain's rail safety as authorities launch an official investigation into the cause of Wednesday's high-speed train collision, which killed at least 68 people and wounded around 100 more, in the country's second fatal rail crash this year.

item.title: EU natural gas prices top €100 for first time since 2022
item.description: As winter approaches, the price of European natural gas has topped €100 per megawatt hour, its highest level since 2022. The EU says it's not worried about supplies, although its storage facilities are only 72 percent full, but warns households of a "difficult" season to come. Also in the show: the UK government tries to cushion the impact of high energy bills, and 200 passengers are stranded in Cambodia after their multi-year cruise was cancelled because of high fuel costs.

item.title: WATCH: How Trump’s economic policies could shape the midterms
item.description: ABC News’ Alex Presha examines voters’ economic concerns, while KPMG chief economist Diane Swonk discusses interest rates, consumer confidence and financial uncertainty.

item.title: Russia woos African leaders at Moscow summit
item.description: In tonight's edition: A summit with nearly two dozen African leaders opens in Moscow, with the Kremlin describing their countries as natural allies against the West. Also, Nigerian investigators say that dozens of detained miners who died in a crowded jail cell screamed for help as jailors ignored their suffering. And ahead of the Youth Olympics in Senegal, Kenya is ramping up support for its female athletes.

item.title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as midterm elections loom
item.description: Markets expect the central bank to hold rates steady for now.

item.title: Historic gains for Arab-majority parties in Israeli election
item.description: Two Arab-majority parties are set to win a historic 19 seats in total, amid a record turnout at the polls in Israel on Tuesday. Voters from the community, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after Israel's creation and who make up around 20 percent of the population, have been enraged by the Netanyahu government's ultra-nationalist Jewish vision for the country and the Palestinian territories. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: Top US federal judge who handled 9/11, Trump, Maduro cases dies aged 92
item.description: Alvin Hellerstein, a top US judge who was handling the trial against deposed Venezuelan leader Nicholas Maduro and previously oversaw lawsuits stemming from the September 11 attacks on the World Trade Centre and multiple cases involving President Donald Trump, died on Wednesday aged 92.

item.title: Bolsonaro's escape to the US: How it happened
item.description: Brazil's defeated right-wing presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro arrived in Florida by private plane Wednesday after fleeing his country in defiance of a court order to surrender his passport. Bolsonaro, who lost a runoff election to incumbent Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on Sunday, is under investigation in Brazil for alleged corruption and money laundering and, with his defeat, is set to lose parliamentary immunity. FRANCE 24's international affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Amid uncertainty over EU aid, Vitalii Kim insists Ukraine has no choice but to fight for motherland
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Vitalii Kim, Minister for Veterans Affairs of Ukraine. “If Europe will not support us, we also will fight because it's our motherland,” says Kim, insisting that Ukraine's determination to resist Russian aggression will endure regardless of the outcome of negotiations over European financial assistance. Yet behind this assertion of national resolve lies a more complex reality: a country confronting not only the immediate pressures of war, but also its mounting psychological, social and institutional consequences.

item.title: Defiant Bolsonaro breaks silence after fleeing Brazil for the US
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro has called himself the "leader of Brazil" - despite losing the presidential election.

item.title: Bolsonaro flees Brazil for US after election defeat
item.description: Flavio Bolsonaro's clandestine escape to the United States bewildered Brazil and triggered a frantic search for his whereabouts. The Supreme Court had ordered the son of jailed ex-leader Jair Bolsonaro to forfeit his passports after his electoral loss on Sunday, amid fears he would leave the country due to ongoing investigations against him. But the defeated right-wing presidential candidate failed to hand them in, choosing instead to flee to the US via Argentina and Ecuador. FRANCE 24's Tim Vickery reports from Rio de Janeiro.

item.title: Which way will Israel break? Netanyahu still in it after election night surprises
item.description: In Israel, the surprises only start with election night. They're still counting ballots in a vote that featured the highest turnout in decades, historic inroads by Arab parties and Benjamin Netanyahu's worst result since 1999. And yet, Israel's longest-serving prime minister still has a path to staying in power. As we await the definitive makeup of the next parliament, our panel breaks out the calculators and pie charts: in what scenario does Netanyahu survive? Is the issue with the right-wing Likud leader or his policies?

item.title: Spain high-speed train crash kills 68, injures over 100
item.description: A high-speed train collision south of Madrid killed 68 people and injured scores more on Wednesday, with the toll likely to rise, authorities said, in one of Europe's deadliest such disasters this century. The second such accident to strike Spain this year will raise fresh questions about the country's rail safety, with the transport minister speaking of an "error" and "inexplicable circumstances" that led to the collision. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Urda, south of Madrid.

item.title: Democratic women could make history in midterm governor and House races
item.description: Candidates and organizations on the left told ABC News both milestones are plausible, but depend on the most competitive races.

item.title: 'Israeli electorate has moved rightward: Many underestimated extent of fracture in Israeli society'
item.description: Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Dr. Shira Efron, RAND's Distinguished Israel Policy Chair. “Many of us, myself included, underestimated the extent of the fracture in Israeli society.” It reflects a political system in which ideological polarisation, the rightward shift of the Jewish electorate and the contested legitimacy of Arab political participation have sharply narrowed the possibilities for coalition-building. Dr. Efron illustrates a political landscape in which Netanyahu’s governing bloc has lost ground, yet still has “more cards, or better cards, to play,” she argues, whether through another election, a national unity government or attempts to draw opposition partners into his orbit.

item.title: Putin woos African leaders as Moscow seeks to expand footprint in Africa
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin sought to woo African leaders and government delegates on Wednesday as they gathered in Moscow for the third Russia-Africa Summit to discuss trade, security, arms deals and grain supplies as part of the Kremlin's strategic efforts to expand its footprint in Africa.

item.title: Man who stabbed 10 on train asked passenger 'do you want to die?', court hears
item.description: A man who stabbed 10 people on a train heading to London asked one passenger "do you want to die?", a court has heard.

item.title: 'Si, se puede': US civil rights icon Dolores Huerta dies at 96
item.description: Influential US labour union co-founder, feminist, and civil rights icon Dolores Huerta died on Wednesday in Bakersfield, California, her family said. Credited with coining the enduring "Si, se puede!" rallying cry later adapted by former US president Barack Obama, Huerta continued her activism on race, poverty, LGBTQ and women's rights issues until the last months of her life.

item.title: LIVE: ABC News Live
item.description: 24/7 coverage of breaking news and live events

item.title: US grants visa to defeated Brazilian presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro
item.description: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro and his immediate family landed in Miami, Florida on Wednesday after he refused to surrender his passports as ordered by his country's Supreme Court in connection with a money-laundering probe. The US State Department on Tuesday announced it had granted entry visas to the senator and his family. France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani explains.

item.title: Ex-FBI agents fighting charges accusing them of lying about Hunter Biden probe
item.description: Attorneys for two former FBI agents charged with lying to Congress about past probes of Hunter Biden are back in court seeking to have the case dismissed.

item.title: WATCH: Where to find the best deals for Thanksgiving
item.description: With Halloween this weekend, many families are already planning for Thanksgiving, and Rebecca Jarvis is at a turkey farm in New Jersey with ways to save on your Thanksgiving meal.

item.description: ABC News’ Will Reeve has the big moments from the extra-inning thriller in Game 4, where the Rays avoided the sweep.

item.description: ABC News contributor Dr. Alok Patel explains the report and what people can do for treatment and prevention.

item.title: WATCH: King tides swamp homes with seawater in South Florida and California coasts
item.description: Some of the highest tides ever recorded in South Florida and California have sent surging seawater into nearby towns – flooding homes on both coasts, and triggering water rescues.

item.title: Cruise ship left stranded in Cambodia after 'soaring fuel costs'
item.description: A luxury cruise ship on a three-year, round-the-world voyage has been forced to suspend the trip in Cambodia due to rising fuel costs, operators have said.

item.title: Knife attacker shot dead by police outside Israeli embassy
item.description: A man carrying knives has been killed by police after attacking an officer outside the Israeli embassy in Belgrade.

item.title: WATCH: Viral explorer finishes 500-mile paddle through Africa
item.description: ABC News' Danny New talks to Ash Dykes, an explorer who kayaked for 500 miles down the Congo Basin in Africa, paddling alongside monkeys and hippos.

item.title: Zookeeper dies after leopard attack
item.description: A woman has died after being attacked by a leopard at the safari park where she spent almost her entire 40-year career.

item.title: WATCH: Jimmy Chin and Jim Morrison talk new Everest documentary
item.description: The filmmaker and ski mountaineer discuss National Geographic's "Everest: The Other Side," documenting a daring climb up Mount Everest's north face and a ski descent.

item.title: WATCH: Widow of man killed on George Washington Bridge demands justice
item.description: Patricia Irvine's husband was fatally shot in an alleged road-rage incident on the upper deck of New York's George Washington Bridge.

item.title: WATCH: Dispute over 3-year-old soccer player goes viral
item.description: A Florida youth soccer organizer called police this past weekend to remove the parents of a 3-year-old boy who the organizer said were being disruptive.

item.title: Mbappe apologises for 'ill-judged' Mao remark after being dropped by Chinese brands
item.description: French footballer Kylian Mbappe has apologised for an "ill-judged" remark about Mao Zedong after being dropped by Chinese brands.
